subject: Model v21a latency surge — request to activate traffic guard / temporary carveout
messages:
From: Sara Green <sara.green@greenbridge.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.io>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95 latency increase for model v21a in prod (US-west)

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

We're seeing a sharp P95 latency increase starting ~08:45 PDT across our US-west traffic that uses model v21a (same traffic pattern we've run for 3 months). Error rates are low, but p95 has moved from ~210ms to ~980ms and user-facing timeouts have started to trigger. Our SLOs are being impacted.

Quick context: we route 60% of traffic to v21a since last week's rollout; variant fallback is enabled but only triggers on failures, not degraded latency. We haven't changed client-side timeouts. Attached is a short perf dump and Grafana snapshot (metrics-snippet.png).

Can Redwood confirm whether you rolled any kernel/path or queuing changes for v21a last night? We need an estimate for mitigation (rollback to v20z, traffic cap, or routing to a cheaper variant). If we need a temporary SLA carveout to allow a controlled rollback, let me know what that entails.

Thanks,
Sara Green
Head of Platform Engineering
GreenBridge Health

Attachments: perf-dump-v21a-20270622.log (stub), metrics-snippet.png (image stub)

Folks — Sara flagged a high-impact P95 spike on v21a for GreenBridge (US-west). Please treat as high-priority.

Initial asks:
- Can infra confirm whether any runtime kernel selection, kv-cache policy, or batching config changed between 02:00-06:00 PDT?
- If the regression is runtime-induced, what's the risk/effort to roll traffic back to v20z for affected customers?
- If rollback is non-trivial, propose a short-term traffic guard (cap to 30% for GreenBridge) and enable optimistic prefix caching for their session types.

Ben/Marcus/Neha — loop me in with a mitigation recommendation within 45m. I'll coordinate the SLA carveout/communication with the customer.

Kimberly Park

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.io>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden p95 latency increase for model v21a in prod (US-west)

Quick findings from initial triage (10:00 PDT):
- No config changes on GreenBridge tenant or client-side.
- We had an automated kernel substitution rollout at 03:14 PDT that targeted a subset of instances running v21a to improve memory locality. Canary metrics passed but the rollout widened at 04:40 PDT.
- The substituted kernel introduces slightly higher per-token scheduling jitter under bursty short-sequence traffic (exactly GreenBridge's profile). This explains p95 spike without error-rate change.

Recommendation:
1) Immediate: enable traffic guard for GreenBridge (cap v21a -> 30% of their traffic) and pin remaining requests to v20z or the stable v21a-kernel-old (alpha tag) if available. This is low-risk and reversible.
2) Short-term: roll back kernel change for GreenBridge pool only (requires infra-scheduling window ~20m).
3) Post-mortem: revert global rollout until kernel fix.

Attachments: v21a-profile-20270622.log (kernel trace stub), metrics-snippet.png (from customer).

Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.io>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Decision: temporary traffic guard + rollback window (authorization request)

Sara — thanks for the data. Here's the planned path so we can move quickly and keep you informed:

Planned actions (need your OK):
- Immediate: we will apply a traffic guard that reduces v21a to 30% of your US-west traffic and route the rest to v20z (stable). This will be applied in ~15 minutes and we will monitor p95 and application-level errors.
- Near-term (within 45m): infra will perform a targeted rollback of the kernel substitution on the GreenBridge pool; expected scheduling window is ~20 minutes and should not cause restarts.
- Customer-facing: Redwood will provide a temporary SLA carveout for the period of the mitigation window (start time and expected duration below). We will also issue a goodwill credit for impacted token costs as part of remediation.

Start (est): 11:20 PDT 2027-06-22
Expected window: 60–90 minutes to confirm stabilization

Please reply with a single-line OK to proceed (Sara) and I'll mark the ticket and notify our Billing/CS teams.

Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Sara — quick update and actions taken:

What we did:
- 11:22 PDT: applied traffic guard limiting v21a to 30% for GreenBridge US-west traffic. Observed P95 drop from ~980ms to ~320ms within 6 minutes.
- 11:45 PDT: executed targeted rollback of kernel substitution for GreenBridge pool (no restarts). Post-rollback p95 stabilized at ~230ms, back within your SLO.
- 15:30 PDT: monitored for longer tail events; no repeat spikes observed.

Next steps we will take (deliverables):
- Post-mortem and RCA scheduled for 2027-06-23 10:00 PDT (invite to follow).
- Rollback playbook and timeline attached (rollback-playbook.pdf).
- We will apply a discretionary one-time billing credit; CS will follow up with specifics and a mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.docx).

If you want us to keep the traffic guard for an extended verification period, say 24–48h, advise and we will keep it in place.

Thanks again for the quick confirmation. Apologies for the disruption — we will prioritize kernel fix and update the rollout gating to be latency-aware.

Kimberly Park
